narrative.overview: A quiet personal study, not a dashboard. One page, skimmed in peace: flat neutral paper tones, generous breathing room, and exactly one signal color that appears only where a number needs to be read at a glance -- the fit score. Nothing competes with the content. No shadows, no chrome, no decoration standing between the reader and the list. The system exists to be opened, skimmed, and closed. It never tries to hold attention past that -- the whole product principle is signal over volume, and the room's calm is the visual expression of that.
keyCharacteristics: Flat surfaces, zero elevation -- depth comes from a single hairline border and a faint tonal shift, never a shadow.
One accent color, used sparingly, reserved for the fit score and the one primary action.
Generous whitespace over density; a centered 900px reading column.
System font stack only -- no webfonts, no display face, nothing to load.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue appears in exactly two places: the fit-score number and the primary button. If a third element wants the accent, that's a sign it doesn't deserve one -- reach for Ink or Soft Graphite instead.

rules.name: The Quiet Ink Rule
rules.body: Everything defaults to Ink or Soft Graphite at normal weight. Weight and color are spent only on the two things worth noticing: the title and the score.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth is tonal and bordered, never cast. If a future component needs to feel "above" the page, lighten its surface and add a hairline border before reaching for a shadow.

dos: Do keep Signal Blue to the fit score and the primary action only (The One Signal Rule).
Do use the tonal-shift + hairline-border pattern for any new "layer above the page" need, instead of a shadow.
Do keep the reasoning line visible by default on every item.
Do reuse the single 10px radius for any new interactive surface.
donts: Don't introduce a shadow anywhere; it breaks the flat-room character established in Elevation & Depth.
Don't add a second accent color -- if something new needs emphasis, it competes with the score for the room's one signal.
Don't repurpose Meadow Green for anything but an affirmative/success state without updating this file first.
Don't add a webfont or display typeface; the system-font stack is a deliberate zero-load choice, matching the local-first product principle.
